name: multiple_dropdowns: A world's fair, also known as a universal exhibition…

request.questionText: A world's fair, also known as a universal exhibition or an expo, is a large global exhibition designed to showcase the achievements of nations. These exhibitions vary in character and are held in different parts of the world at a specific site for a period of time, typically between three and six months. The fairs.csv file contains information on 70 world's fairs, including these variables: name and theme --- used to describe the fair city and country --- location where fair was held month and year --- dates for when the fair began visitors --- number of visitors in millions cost --- cost in millions of U.S. dollars Imagine that you are an international event planner working with historical data on some of the world's grandest gatherings. You want to predict expenditures in terms of the scale of the event (e.g., size of crowds): Fit a linear model to explore the extent to which the number of fair visitors explains variation in event cost. Considering how sample results might generalize to a broader population of large international events, use bootstrapping with 10000 iterations to generate 95% confidence intervals for model estimates and model fit statistics. Use these results to fill in the blanks below with the best answer: If we converted measurement units for cost from U.S. Dollars to Chinese Yuan, the R-squared estimate for these variables would [ Select ] ["change", "not change"] . We are 95% confident that the typical model error we expect in predicting cost from visitors is not greater than approximately [ Select ] ["$26 million", "$870 million", "$430 million", "$66 million", "$50 million", "$1.1 billion"] . The association between the number of visitors and cost is [ Select ] ["not statistically significant", "practically significant", "statistically significant", "not practically significant"] with 95% confidence because zero is NOT included in the interval as a plausible value for the population [ Select ] ["estimate", "estimand"] .
